scenarios: QA bundle construction admits source-checkout scripts into the supposedly source-blind bundle.
Native proof references are validated only for repository containment, so non-Evidence repository files can be used as proof.
Independent role execution is not completed in this attempt.

findings.failureMode: The QA allowlist excludes only src/ and .git, so tracked scripts/ (including scripts/agent-role and other source-bearing files) are copied into qa-bundle. The delivered bundle therefore exposes source and a role-control interface to source-blind QA, violating the required read-only public-artifact boundary and enabling prompt/source leakage.
findings.rationale: The candidate diff explicitly filters with qaAllowedPath that permits scripts/, then copies every permitted tracked file. The generated bundle is consequently not source-blind.
findings.correction: Use an explicit public-artifact allowlist (docs, schemas, API reports, procedures, and the intended launcher only), reject scripts/, tooling, package source, and any executable not explicitly declared; add a fixture asserting scripts/ are absent.

findings.failureMode: nativeProofRef is accepted when it points to any regular repository file under root; it is not required to reside under the Work Item Evidence directory or attempt scope. An attester can point at tracked source/configuration as native proof, making proof provenance forgeable and bypassing the documented repository-relative Evidence requirement.
findings.rationale: recordExternalAttestation calls validateEvidenceReference(context.root, envelope.nativeProofRef, ...), whose visible contract only checks repository containment/digest.
findings.correction: Resolve and enforce nativeProofRef beneath the current Work Item evidence/attempt directory before reading, reject source and shared-state paths, and bind the stored proof reference to the attempt manifest.
